E1.text: May 15 – Sejong the Great of Joseon, ruler of Korea (d.

E6.title: Sejong the Great
E6.text: Yi To was born on the 10th day, 4th month of 1397 in Chunsubang, Hanyang (Seoul), Joseon as the third son of father Grand Prince Chŏngan and Princess Chŏngnyŏng.

E7.title: Sejong the Great
E7.text: Yi To's father was the fifth son of the founding and reigning king of Joseon, Taejo (r.

E10.title: Sejong the Great
E10.text: — Veritable Records of Sejong, 17th day, 11th month of 1443

E25.title: Sejong the Great
E25.text: Sejong was born the third son of the future King Taejong (r.

E27.title: Sejong the Great
E27.text: He was regarded as gifted, moreso than the troubled crown prince Grand Prince Yangnyŏng.

E28.title: Sejong the Great
E28.text: In mid-1418, Yangnyŏng was deposed and Sejong made the crown prince.

E29.title: Sejong the Great
E29.text: Months later, Taejong abdicated and Sejong was crowned king.

E30.title: Sejong the Great
E30.text: Taejong served as king emeritus until his death in 1422.

E34.title: Sejong the Great
E34.text: Yi To was born five years after the founding of Joseon.

E35.title: Sejong the Great
E35.text: His father, Grand Prince Chŏngan, had played a major role in the dynasty's establishment.

E36.title: Sejong the Great
E36.text: In 1398, Chŏngan became embroiled in a succession crisis.

E37.title: Sejong the Great
E37.text: He launched the First Strife of the Princes, which resulted in the installment of one of his brothers as King Jeongjong (r.

E39.title: Sejong the Great
E39.text: After suppressing a coup in the Second Strife of the Princes, Jeongjong abdicated the throne in favor of Chŏngan, who became King Taejong (r.

E41.title: Sejong the Great
E41.text: "Sejong" is the name by which he is most widely known.

E42.title: Sejong the Great
E42.text: It is a temple name: a posthumous title that was given to him on the 19th day, 3rd month of 1450.

E43.title: Sejong the Great
E43.text: Historian Gari Ledyard roughly translates its meaning as "epochal ancestor".

E44.title: Sejong the Great
E44.text: Sejong's birth name was Yi To (이도; 李祹).

E45.title: Sejong the Great
E45.text: In the 2nd month of 1408, Yi To was granted the name "Ch'ungnyŏng" (충녕; 忠寧) and the title "Prince" (군; 君).

E46.title: Sejong the Great
E46.text: In the 5th month of 1413, Ch'ungnyŏng was granted the title "Grand Prince" (대군; 大君).

E47.title: Sejong the Great
E47.text: On the 27th day, 6th month of 1418, Ch'ungnyŏng was granted the courtesy name "Wŏnjŏng" (원정; 元正).

E48.title: Sejong the Great
E48.text: On the 10th day, 8th month of 1418, Taejong abdicated and 21-year-old Ch'ungnyŏng (henceforth Sejong) ascended the throne at the hall Geunjeongjeon in the palace Gyeongbokgung.

E49.title: Sejong the Great
E49.text: Taejong, as king emeritus, would continue to exert great influence over Sejong until the former's death on the 10th day, 5th month of 1422.

E50.title: Sejong the Great
E50.text: Taejong had veto power on all decisions and maintained tight control over the military.

E51.title: Sejong the Great
E51.text: On the 26th day, 10th month of 1421, Sejong designated his son Yi Hyang as crown prince.

E53.title: Sejong the Great
E53.text: Sejong (Korean: 세종; Hanja: 世宗; May 15, 1397 – April 8, 1450), commonly known as Sejong the Great (세종대왕; 世宗大王), was the fourth monarch of the Koreanic state Joseon.

E54.title: Sejong the Great
E54.text: He ruled from 1418 to his death in 1450.

E55.title: Sejong the Great
E55.text: He is widely regarded as the greatest king in Korean history, and is particularly remembered for the creation of Hangul, the native alphabet of the Korean language.
